previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for severe abdominal pain, elevated white blood cell count, and recent constipation. Initial imaging showed no acute abdominal process but revealed severe hepatomegaly and stool burden. A stool test confirmed Clostridium difficile infection, which was treated with oral vancomycin and IV metronidazole. Her leukocytosis resolved, diarrhea improved, and abdominal pain subsided. Amitiza was discontinued due to contribution to diarrhea, and diuretics were held due to hypotension but planned for outpatient restart. She remained stable, with controlled hepatic encephalopathy and ongoing management of iron deficiency anemia. She was discharged home with a tapering course of vancomycin, instructions to follow up with her liver and primary care teams, and guidance on when to resume diuretics.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with hx of EtOH cirrhosis (CHILDS B, MELD 12) c/b varices, 
encephalopathy, and diuretic-controlled asciites, presenting 
with abdominal pain, fever and encephalopathy.

# Presumed Sepsis / SBP: Fever, abdominal pain, hypotension, 
tachycardia. No ascites for paracentesis to diagnose SBP 
definitively. UA bland. CXR w/ only some atelectasis. Moderate 
hypotension with SBP in low-mid ___ on ___ which was fluid 
responsive (received 2L LR). Ceftriaxone started on ___ for 
presumed SBP. C.diff sent but not run due to formed stool so PO 
vancomycin discontinued on ___. Patient had no further fevers 
after her initial value of 100.8 on ___ and her blood pressure 
stabilized on ___. Transitioned to levofloxacin at discharge 
and will complete 48 hours of this antibiotic as an outpatient. 
Blood cultures were NGTD at discharge.

# Encephalopathy: Most likely hepatic encephalopathy, potential 
triggers for which include SBP (see above), UTI (bland UA), 
other infection (no localizing symptoms), medication effect (no 
new meds at last discharge), GI bleed (no melena, negative stool 
guiaic), or idiopathic decompensation. Patient did exhibit 1.5 
pt drop in Hgb over first 24 hours of her admission but this was 
in the setting of receiving ~3L IVF and it stabilized 
thereafter. Stool was formed and not suitable for C.diff assay. 
Lactulose was given Q2H and titrated to improvement of 
encephalopathy with excellent effect. Patient was A&Ox1 on 
admission but A&Ox3 by ___.

# Abdominal Pain: Longstanding issue with many prior admission 
with extensive work-up (normal EGD, H.Pylori negative, celiac 
negative). Current thought is either constipation-predominant 
IBS versus a consequence of a T10 paraspinal mass seen on a 
recent abdominal MRI from ___. Her current imaging is 
unremarkable and unchanged from prior. During her ___ 
admission at ___ she had C.difficile for which she was started on 
vancomycin and her lubiprostone was discontinued. Plan is to 
start linactolide as an outpatient at ___ follow up appointment 
(this medication requires prior approval).

DLP:  1503 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: 

The heart size is normal. Bibasilar atelectasis. No pericardial or pleural
effusion.

ABDOMEN:

The liver has heterogeneous enhancement with a nodular contour and atrophy of
the left hepatic lobe, consistent with cirrhosis.  The gallbladder is
anteriorly displaced and otherwise unremarkable without stone or wall edema.
Intra and extrahepatic bile ducts, pancreas, and adrenal glands are normal.
The spleen is enlarged, measuring 13.1 cm. A subcentimeter renal lesion is
present in the left kidney. The kidneys otherwise enhance homogeneously
without striated nephrogram to suggest pyelonephritis. There is no calcified
renal stone or hydronephrosis.

The distal esophagus and stomach are unremarkable. Small and large bowel
enhance homogeneously and have a normal course and caliber. The appendix is
normal.

Several small nodes are identified in the porta hepatis, similar to prior. No
pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph node.  19 x 12 mm
retromediastinal enhancing soft tissue density (4:9) is stable, lateral to the
T10 vertebral body. The portal and intra-abdominal systemic vasculature are
normal.  No pneumoperitoneum, or free abdominal fluid. Fat containing ventral
hernia.

PELVIS:  The bladder and terminal ureters are normal.  The uterus contains
multiple fibroids, including a 5.2 x 4.0 cm right cervical fibroid.  No pelvic
side-wall or inguinal lymphadenopathy. No free pelvic fluid or inguinal
hernia.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: No focal lytic or sclerotic lesion concerning for
malignancy.

IMPRESSION: 

1. No acute intra-abdominal process. No evidence of renal stone,
hydronephrosis, or pyelonephritis.

2. Fibroid uterus.

3. Stable 19 x 12 mm retromediastinal soft tissue density, differential for
which includes nerve sheath tumor, extramedullary hematopoiesis, or an unusual
lymph node.
